public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 486: Logarithmic density for sets avoiding modular subsets

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/486](https://www.erdosproblems.com/486)
* [Wa26] Wang, S., *A proposed solution to Erdős Problem 486* (2026),
  https://github.com/ShouqiaoW/erdos/blob/main/486/paper.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos486

/--
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, and for each $n \in A$ choose some
$X_n \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Let
$B = \{m \in \mathbb{N} : m \not\in X_n \pmod{n} \text{ for all } n \in A \text{ with } m > n\}$.
Must $B$ have a logarithmic density?

The set $A$ is encoded by taking $X_n = \emptyset$ for $n \notin A$. Only positive moduli
$n$ are considered, since $\mathbb{Z}/0\mathbb{Z} = \mathbb{Z}$ would allow $B$ to be an
arbitrary set.

The answer is no: Wang [Wa26] (with GPT-5.6) constructed a congruence system whose survivor set
$B$ has lower logarithmic density at most $177/200$ and upper logarithmic density at least
$49/50$. The first linked formal proof establishes this for the real-cutoff normalisation
$\frac{1}{\log x}\sum_{m < x, m \in B} \frac{1}{m}$ with the moduli restricted to $A$; the
second derives the statement below (`Set.HasLogDensity`, all moduli) from it.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos486.lean#L20",
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
  "https://github.com/Konamiu/formal-conjectures/blob/c69df0584ca9767090f5a68c8f09f1ff3c93ab80/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/486.lean#L39"]
theorem erdos_486 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ X : (n : ℕ) → Set (ZMod n),
      ∃ d, {m : ℕ | ∀ n, 0 < n → n < m → (m : ZMod n) ∉ X n}.HasLogDensity d := by
  sorry

end Erdos486

reformulations.difference: The source specifies a set A of positive moduli, residue sets indexed only by A, positive survivors, and real-cutoff averages over m < x. Lean instead quantifies over families at all natural-number indices, activates only positive moduli, includes 0 among the survivors, and uses Set.HasLogDensity with integer cutoffs m ≤ N.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Extend the source family by the empty set outside A; conversely, take A to be all positive integers. The resulting Lean survivor set is the source survivor set with 0 adjoined, which does not change reciprocal sums because (0 : ℝ)⁻¹ = 0. For real x tending to infinity, put N = ⌈x⌉ − 1: the numerator over m < x equals that over m ≤ N, and log N / log x tends to 1. Conversely, evaluate the real-cutoff averages at x = N + 1. Thus both density definitions have exactly the same limits. The full equivalence between the literal False ↔ ∀ X, ∃ d, ... statement and the negation of the source's universal assertion was proved as Review486.full_statement_equiv in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, with only standard axioms.

review.notes: The fixed answer(False), strict activation n < m, positive-modulus restriction and quoted quantitative bounds agree with Wang's paper. Boundary checks covered empty/full residue families, moduli 0 and 1, and the zero reciprocal term. The cited standalone proof's negative and quantitative theorems were replayed successfully; #print axioms reported only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/486 remained blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive user-agent headers, and a readable proxy was rate-limited. Consequently its live status and remarks were not independently read; the other cited sources support the statement and recorded solved status.
